svg.title: From Loss Intake to Collected Restoration Invoice
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-evidence-to-collection; chart type: process_flow; title: From Loss Intake to Collected Restoration Invoice; subtitle: Five accountable handoffs connect field evidence with job economics.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Stage numbers indicate sequence, not conversion rates. Restoration contract billings are operator revenue; total insured property value and insurer claim reserves are not.; caption: Dispatch, photo documentation, and job-cost tracking automate handoffs without deciding coverage or negotiating policy rights.; stages: label: Qualify the loss; value: Intake and jurisdiction review; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Record property address, water source or fire damage, occupancy, access authority, emergency hazards, and required contractor or remediation credentials.; label: Authorize the work; value: Signed scope and payment terms; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Obtain the customer's work authorization, explain deductible responsibilities, and document payment terms without promising insurer coverage.; label: Mitigate and measure; value: Time-stamped field evidence; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Assign drying equipment and responsible technicians; record temperature, relative humidity, humidity ratio, material moisture, equipment days, and dated photographs using applicable IICRC documentation practices.; label: Estimate and reconcile; value: Supported Xactimate scope; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Tie quantities, labor, equipment, and supplements to actual work and supporting evidence. Route policy interpretation or claim negotiation outside contractor scope.; label: Invoice and collect; value: Receivable and margin closeout; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Submit an itemized invoice, track customer and insurer remittance paths, resolve contractual scope discrepancies, and reconcile receipts against job costs without unauthorized public adjusting.

text.title: From Loss Intake to Collected Restoration Invoice
text.tspan: From Loss Intake to Collected Restoration Invoice

circle.title: label: Qualify the loss; value: Intake and jurisdiction review; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Record property address, water source or fire damage, occupancy, access authority, emergency hazards, and required contractor or remediation credentials.

text.title: Record property address, water source or fire damage, occupancy, access authority, emergency hazards, and required contractor or remediation credentials.

circle.title: label: Authorize the work; value: Signed scope and payment terms; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Obtain the customer's work authorization, explain deductible responsibilities, and document payment terms without promising insurer coverage.

text.title: Obtain the customer's work authorization, explain deductible responsibilities, and document payment terms without promising insurer coverage.

circle.title: label: Mitigate and measure; value: Time-stamped field evidence; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Assign drying equipment and responsible technicians; record temperature, relative humidity, humidity ratio, material moisture, equipment days, and dated photographs using applicable IICRC documentation practices.

text.title: Assign drying equipment and responsible technicians; record temperature, relative humidity, humidity ratio, material moisture, equipment days, and dated photographs using applicable IICRC documentation practices.

circle.title: label: Estimate and reconcile; value: Supported Xactimate scope; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Tie quantities, labor, equipment, and supplements to actual work and supporting evidence. Route policy interpretation or claim negotiation outside contractor scope.

text.title: Tie quantities, labor, equipment, and supplements to actual work and supporting evidence. Route policy interpretation or claim negotiation outside contractor scope.

circle.title: label: Invoice and collect; value: Receivable and margin closeout; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Submit an itemized invoice, track customer and insurer remittance paths, resolve contractual scope discrepancies, and reconcile receipts against job costs without unauthorized public adjusting.

text.title: Submit an itemized invoice, track customer and insurer remittance paths, resolve contractual scope discrepancies, and reconcile receipts against job costs without unauthorized public adjusting.
Assumptions: Stage numbers indicate sequence, not conversion rates. Restoration contract billings are operator revenue; total insured property value and insurer claim reserves are not.

property value and insurer claim reserves are not.
